s.how: Heat the oven to 200C. Pull the stalks from 20 button mushrooms and chop them finely. Mix the stalks with 150g softened cream cheese, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 40g grated parmesan and chopped parsley. Fill each mushroom cap. Mix 30g breadcrumbs with 1 tbsp melted butter and press on top. Bake 15 minutes until bubbling and golden.

s.note: Friday's desk, all strictly by the book
s.how: Warm 180ml milk with 30g butter and 2 tbsp caster sugar, add 7g yeast and 1 egg, then mix into 350g plain flour with a pinch of salt. Knead 5 minutes and prove 1 hour. Roll into 30 small balls and prove 20 minutes. Fry at 175C for 2 minutes, turning, until golden. Whisk 200g icing sugar with 3 tbsp milk and 1 tsp vanilla, dip the warm doughnuts and set on a rack.

m.how: Cut 1.2kg pork shoulder into chunks, rub with cumin, oregano and salt and braise with 1 orange, 3 garlic cloves and 250ml water at 160C for 2.5 hours. Shred, crisp in the pan and serve in 16 corn tortillas with diced onion, coriander and lime.

w.how: Bake 2 sheets puff pastry pricked and weighted at 200C for 15 minutes. Whisk 1L milk, 6 egg yolks, 150g sugar, 90g cornflour and 2 tsp vanilla over medium heat until very thick. Spread between the pastry in a lined tin, chill 4 hours, ice with 200g icing sugar mixed with a little water and cut into squares.

d.n: Just the facts cold brew tonic
d.note: Friday takes his coffee black, and nothing extra
d.how: The night before, stir 100g coarsely ground coffee into 800ml cold water in a jug, cover and leave in the fridge for 12 to 16 hours. Strain through a paper filter. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, pour in 150ml tonic water each, then slowly pour 100ml cold brew over the top so it layers. Squeeze a strip of orange peel over each glass and drop it in.
